title: Truncated sentence recovery playbook (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference + working notes for identifying and repairing truncated sentences in user-contributed text. This is a scratchpad: heuristics, example-driven rules, TODOs, and an initial pipeline sketch.

Context and motivation:
- We keep seeing partial sentences in multiple datasets (chat logs, customer feedback, webhook payloads) that break downstream tokenizers and context windows.
- Truncation happens for different reasons: frontend character limits, network drops, copy/paste artifacts, CSV cell clipping, and heuristic redactors.
- Goal: detect high-confidence truncation, recover where possible (reconstruction or stitch), and flag ambiguous cases for human review.

Quick definitions (working):
- soft-truncation: sentence ends abruptly with mid-word break or punctuation that suggests cut-off ("I was trying to upda").
- hard-truncation: explicit sentinel like "[TRUNCATED]" or trailing ellipses with no closing punctuation.
- clipped-field: CSV/TSV cell where surrounding context indicates missing suffix (often at field length boundary).

High-level detection signals (ranked):
1) token-level signals
   - ends_with_incomplete_token: final token contains non-letter suffix (e.g., ends with lowercase fragment, dash, single letter)
   - last_char_is_alpha_but_word_is_short: final token length <=3 and not a known short word list ("an","to","the" etc.)
2) punctuation signals
   - trailing hyphen, colon, open paren, unmatched quotes, or single unpaired bracket
   - ends with comma but sentence lacks coordinating continuation
3) length + language model score
   - very short sentence ending mid-phrase (e.g., length <10 chars + LM perplexity of appended <context> rises)
4) structural context
   - adjacent row/turn has continuation patterns (next row starts with lowercased word that aligns to flow)
   - metadata flags: client-side truncation header, HTTP 408/413 in logs near timestamp
5) sentinel tokens
   - presence of explicit markers ("...","[TRUNC]","<trunc>")

Repair strategies (ordered by safety):
A) no-op + label: mark as truncated and route to human if high-impact data (preserve original).
B) stitch adjacent turns: if dataset is chat or sequential logs, attempt concatenation with previous/next messages when timestamps/author match expected patterns.
   - rules: only stitch if same speaker OR next turn's first token is lowercase and first sentence token aligns syntactically.
C) LM-based completion (constrained): generate 1–2 plausible completions with beam size 5, then score candidates by: consistency with previous/next tokens, minimal hallucination (prefer continuations that reuse tokens in nearby context), and token-prob threshold. Add "reconstructed_from_model" tag.
D) dictionary/phrase heuristics: for common clipped suffixes (URLs, emails, file paths) attempt canonical completion patterns (e.g., if ends with "http://exa" -> try to expand to known domain patterns or mark for QA).
E) pattern substitution: replace broken quotes/brackets and re-evaluate sentence boundary detection.

Examples and notes (real-ish samples):
- "I went to the st" -> low-confidence LM completion: "I went to the store." If adjacent tokens mention "milk" -> higher confidence.
- "Error: failed to parse header: X-Request-" -> likely header truncation; prefer stitch with subsequent log lines.
- "Can you please update the" -> ambiguous; don't auto-complete for user-facing outputs. Flag for human review, suggest top-3 LM completions in UI.
- "Download at https://re" -> treat as URL truncation; try heuristics: if domain prefix present elsewhere in dataset, reuse full domain.

Heuristic rules (conservative parameters to start):
- Only auto-complete via LM when: final token length >=3 OR final char is letter AND probability mass over next-token predictions > 0.6 for top candidate.
- When stitching, require timestamp gap < 10s for chat logs or row index adjacent for table exports.
- Don’t auto-complete if original text contains user PII patterns (SSN, CC numbers) — escalate to human.
- For items with quotation marks: if opening quote present and no closing quote, attempt to find closing quote in next N=3 rows before reconstructing.

Pipeline sketch (component-level):
1) ingestion -> normalize whitespace, decode escaped unicode, preserve raw_text field.
2) detector -> apply regex battery + LM-based anomaly detector to score truncation probability (0.0-1.0).
3) classifier -> risk bands: low (just label), med (stitch or heuristic completion), high (LM completion candidate generation but store alternatives), critical (human).
4) reconstructor -> (stitcher, pattern-expander, LM-completer) produce at most 3 candidate repairs plus provenance metadata.
5) reviewer queue -> UI snippet shows original, candidates, confidence, provenance; allow accept/reject/modify; accepted repairs write to clean_text field with audit trail.

Regex and quick detectors (notes):
- incomplete word: /[a-zA-Z]+-[a-zA-Z]*$/ ; trailing hyphen likely concatenation cut
- open bracket: /(?:\(|\[|\{)[^\)\]\}]*$/ -> unclosed bracket at end
- url-cut: /(https?:\/\/[^\s]{3,}[^\s]*)$/ detect if last token starts with http and length <10
- unusual whitespace end: /\s+$/ — sometimes indicates CSV cut due to field trimming

Label schema for humans (simple):
- truncated_bool: yes/no
- truncation_type: soft|hard|clipped|unknown
- recovery_action: none|stitch|lm_complete|heuristic|human_fix
- candidate_texts: pipe-separated short list (store separately in DB in practice)
- reviewer_notes: free text

Evaluation and metrics (how we measure success):
- precision@auto-repair: percent of auto-applied repairs that were accepted by reviewers in sample
- review-load reduction: fraction fewer items routed to humans after deploying conservative rules
- downstream error delta: change in tokenizer/parsing errors after fixes (should go down)

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- Does platform allow storing multiple candidate variants per row? DB schema question. (JIRA-LABEL-291)
- Build small human-in-the-loop UI mockup for QA team — need quick accept/reject flow with keyboard shortcuts.
- Run a corpus analysis to estimate prevalence by source (chat vs support tickets vs CSV imports).
- Edge case: bilingual lines where LM completion might erroneously switch language. Need language detection guard.
- Decide retention policy for original_text vs clean_text for compliance.

Quick experiment plan (next 2 weeks):
- Sample 5k random records across sources; run detector; hand-label 500 for gold.
- Implement conservative stitcher + pattern expander; auto-apply only low-risk repairs.
- Set up review queue and measure acceptance rate after 7 days.

Notes to self: keep heuristics conservative at first. prioritize auditability and provenance. Capture why a repair was chosen (stitch vs LM vs heuristic) in metadata. When in doubt, route to human.

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers (to paste into UI):
- Is the candidate preserving original intent?
- Any added PII or hallucinated facts?
- If LM completion used, does it reuse anchor tokens from context?
- If stitched, check speaker continuity and timestamps.

End of scratchpad. Will iteratively refine with Jae and SRE logs once we have sample counts.
